A sign gestalt expectation is formed when an agent associates a sign-object with a potential goal-object through known pathways. This forms a probabilistic map of possible outcomes, which is updated iteratively via Bayesian inference. Inference occurs not just from direct observation but also from hierarchical abstraction of past experiences. The dual nature of perception and memory allows for both immediate reaction and anticipatory planning. Failure modes arise when sign-object relations lack predictive power or when hierarchical structures collapse under complexity. These primitives form the basis for constructing dynamic models of decision-making in uncertain environments.
